flags.source_says: Key (c); (d) asserted true: 'Raising correlation reduces diversification and fattens the tail, so credit VaR rises.' Source trap text says the item was rebuilt from a version where both (c) and (d) were false.
flags.derivation: n=20, p=1%, zero recovery, 95% level. Base: P(0)=0.8179, P(<=1)=0.9831 -> q95 = 1 default, VaR = 50-10 = 40 (correct). Under a one-factor Gaussian copula (python integration) P(>=2 defaults) peaks at only ~4.1% (asset rho ~0.45), so q95 stays at 1 and VaR stays 40 for rho up to ~0.8; for rho >= ~0.85 P(0) > 95% so q95 = 0 and VaR = -10 (floored 0). Beta-binomial with default correlation 0.01-0.6 gives the same: P(>=2) max ~4.6%, P(0) rises to 0.97. So raising correlation never increases the 95% credit VaR here and eventually lowers it (same threshold effect the set itself explains in CR-T2-16). Statement (d) is therefore false as well as (c).
